title: Policy Playground + Admin Simulator: adaptive RBAC v2 evaluator and enriched audit hooks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a focused RBAC v2 policy evaluation engine component that powers a developer-facing Policy Playground (sandbox) and an Admin Simulator UI for the Console, plus a light-weight authorization middleware for API/runtime paths. The component must support intent scoring, contextual explainability traces, SAML role mapping enrichment, and audit record augmentation for downstream log sinks.

Scope:
- Core policy runner (deterministic, reproducible evaluation) that can run in-process for Console and as a sidecarless middleware for API/runtime requests.
- Policy Playground: an interactive sandbox where engineers and admins can submit simulated requests, toggle principal attributes (SAML groups, token scopes, dedicated vs hosted flags), and see the full decision trace, including scoring and which rules fired.
- Admin Simulator integration into Console: enable admins to preview effective entitlements for a user or service token without changing live policies. Simulator output must include suggested mitigations for overly-broad grants.
- Audit enrichment: augment decision logs with SAML assertion metadata, role provenance, evaluation latency, and intent score; send to both internal audit pipeline and customer-configured sinks.
- Authorization middleware: a minimal dependency runtime interceptor that enforces decisions, supports fast-cached allow/deny, and fallbacks to a degrade-mode when policy-store is unreachable.
- Explainability API: a compact JSON explain format for use by Console, Policy Playground, and incident triage dashboards.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not replace the long-term policy shard/cluster design; it's an incremental, backwards-compatible runner and UX surface.
- Not implementing a full OPA/rego migration; policy language stays current RBAC v2 DSL with staged boolean operators and intent scoring extensions.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- We choose a single-threaded deterministic evaluator to avoid non-deterministic explain traces; heavier throughput will rely on multiple runner instances rather than worker-thread mutation.
- Cache TTLs: short TTL (500ms) for token-attribute caches to keep latency low while capturing attribute churn in SSO mappings.
- Intent scoring: additive micro-scores from rule matches; deterministic tie-breakers required for consistent audit messages. This sacrifices granularity for reproducibility.
- Risk: enriching audit logs increases payload sizes. We'll provide sampling and compression config per project in the audit pipeline to mitigate cost.
acceptance_criteria: Console admin can open Policy Playground and run simulated request with at least 5 adjustable principal attributes
Simulator returns deterministic explain trace (same inputs => same decision + same explain JSON) across restarts
Middleware enforces allow/deny decisions with <8ms median overhead on p99-optimized path for cached decisions
Audit records include: decision id, rule trace, intent score, SAML role mapping metadata, evaluation latency, and runner version
Fallback behavior: when policy-store unavailable, middleware returns configured degrade-mode (fail-open or fail-closed) per route and emits a high-severity audit event
End-to-end integration tests exist and are included in runtime-1.23 release branch
